---
title: "Cleaning of position reports"
description: "How OPDI removes repeated, impossible and isolated values from the position reports before any flight-list column or event is computed."
---

## In one sentence

Cleaning finds the values of the position reports that cannot be trusted and
**empties** them (the value becomes missing, the report is kept) before any
column of the flight list or any event is computed.

## What it needs

The tracks (see [Tracks and flight identity](tracks.qmd)): seven fields of
each report are cleaned, namely latitude, longitude, barometric altitude
(from air pressure), geometric altitude (from satellite navigation), ground
speed, heading and vertical rate. The identity fields (address, call sign,
time) are never changed.

## How it is computed

Six stages run on each track, in this order.

1. **Duplicates.** Of two reports of one track at the same time, the one
   received last is kept.
2. **Impossible coordinates.** A latitude outside −90° to 90° or a longitude
   outside −180° to 180° is emptied.
3. **Repeated values.** ADS-B sends position and speed in separate messages,
   and OpenSky repeats the last value until a new one arrives, so a value equal
   to the one before was often not measured again:
   - latitude and longitude are emptied when the position was not updated
     (each state vector records when its position was last updated; without
     that time, when neither changed);
   - the barometric altitude is emptied when neither the position was updated
     nor the altitude changed;
   - ground speed, heading and vertical rate are emptied together when none of
     the three changed.

   The first report of a track is never a repeat.
4. **Spikes.** For each field, the rate of change between two consecutive
   values still present (first difference) and the change of that rate
   (second difference) are compared with a limit. A value is emptied when it
   takes part in at least **two** over-limit changes of the same kind: the
   middle of a spike takes part in the jump up and the jump down, while a real
   step change takes part in only one and is kept.

   | Field | Limit on first difference | Limit on second difference |
   |---|---|---|
   | Barometric altitude | 200 ft/s | 50 ft/s |
   | Geometric altitude | 200 ft/s | 150 ft/s |
   | Vertical rate | 1,500 ft/min per second | 1,000 ft/min per second |
   | Ground speed | 12 kt/s | 10 kt/s |
   | Heading | 12°/s | 10°/s |
   | Latitude and longitude | 0.01°/s | 0.06°/s |

5. **Isolated values.** A value with no other value of the same field within
   20 s on either side cannot be confirmed and is emptied.
6. **Silences.** A silence of 300 s or more starts a new segment of the
   track, so that later steps never interpolate across it.

The event detectors then also leave aside a barometric altitude below
−2,000 ft or above 60,000 ft.

Three things are deliberately **not** done, because the PRC Data Challenges
found that they made results worse: filling gaps with invented positions,
removing positions disturbed by satellite-navigation jamming, and correcting
speeds with weather-model wind.

## Based on

The trajectory cleaning of the winning solution of the
[2024 PRC Data Challenge](../data-challenges.qmd), by Alligier and Gianazza
(ENAC, team likable_jelly): the stages, the two-vote rule for spikes and the 20 s
rule for isolated values. The three things not done are documented negative
results of the 2024 and 2025 challenges.

## What is published

Nothing directly: the cleaned reports are not published. Every flight-list
column, event and measurement is computed from them.

## Use cases

- **Reading OPDI events**: a missing altitude or position on an event often
  comes from a value emptied here; it is "no data", not an estimate.
- **Reproducing OPDI** from the OpenSky archive with the same cleaning.

## Limitations

A spoofed position that does not jump (a frozen position) passes the
cleaning, and a value emptied here is not replaced. See
[Limitations: tracks](../limitations.qmd#lim-tracks).

## Availability and accuracy

Not measured as a published item: cleaning affects the availability and
accuracy of every other item.
